globalRelease.label: Pre-release hardening
globalRelease.summary: SparkEngine is source-usable and feature-rich, but it is not yet a fully ready engine release. Required CI can mask failures, no versioned release exists, shipping artifacts are not signed or attested, platform and renderer support is not certified, most genre modules remain prototypes, and production networking and operations are incomplete.
definition: Every blocking release gate is passing at the same source commit.
Required builds and tests fail closed and attach machine-readable evidence.
Primary platform, renderer, editor, packaged runtime, and SDK workflows pass end to end.
Every advertised game module meets its declared release profile or is explicitly labeled as a prototype/template.
Versioned Shipping artifacts are reproducible, signed, checksummed, scanned, attested, installable, uninstallable, and rollback-tested.
Security, performance, crash recovery, compatibility, documentation, legal, and operations gates have named evidence and owners.
The repository-generated site bundle and handoff match the exact tested commit.

statusPromotionRules: Implementation, verification, support, and release are independent dimensions; never infer one from another.
A capability cannot be release-ready while a required gate is not passing or a blocking work item is open.
A passing test must execute production source or a packaged binary; mirror-only, tautological, or mock-only tests cannot promote readiness.
Every public numeric claim resolves through a generated metric with an evidence path.
Every readiness promotion includes source, tests, CI evidence, documentation, limitations, and website impact in the same change.
Production-ready wording is forbidden until the global release state is ready at the displayed commit.
If live publication fails, the website labels the last valid bundle stale or unavailable; it never silently calls the fallback current.

capabilities.name: Windows host
capabilities.summary: Windows is the broadest and intended primary host, with MSVC, the editor, D3D11, and packaging projects present.
limitations: No same-commit Shipping certification, signing, install/uninstall, upgrade, or rollback evidence is published.

website.title: The primary host candidate
bullets: MSVC and Windows platform paths exist
D3D11 and editor depth are strongest here
Shipping, signing, installer, upgrade, and rollback gates remain open

capabilities.name: Linux host
capabilities.summary: Linux build, sanitizer, headless, OpenGL, and Vulkan paths exist, but the supported driver/package/runtime matrix is not release-certified.
limitations: No installable release package or declared driver matrix
Renderer and packaged content parity remain incomplete

website.title: Portable foundations under certification
bullets: GCC and Clang paths exist
Sanitizers and headless execution provide useful evidence
Drivers, rendering parity, packaging, and support policy remain open

capabilities.name: macOS host
capabilities.summary: macOS build work exists, while Metal, packaging, signing, notarization, and end-to-end runtime evidence remain incomplete.
limitations: Metal is not a complete certified renderer
No notarized release package or packaged golden-scene evidence

website.title: An experimental host path
bullets: Build and platform entry points exist
Metal parity and packaged runtime proof are incomplete
Signing and notarization remain release blockers

capabilities.name: Mobile platforms
capabilities.summary: Touch and quality-scaling foundations do not constitute an iOS or Android deployment backend.
limitations: No complete platform layer, build pipeline, store package, device matrix, or lifecycle validation

website.title: Framework work, not a shipping target
bullets: Input foundations exist
Native lifecycle, graphics, packaging, devices, and stores remain unproven

capabilities.name: VR / OpenXR
capabilities.summary: VR is an interface/framework surface without a completed OpenXR runtime path.
limitations: No runtime initialization, device validation, interaction profile, stereo renderer certification, or packaged headset test

website.title: A framework stub
bullets: Interface concepts exist
OpenXR runtime, stereo rendering, input, performance, and device proof do not

capabilities.name: Console platforms
capabilities.summary: PlayStation and Xbox support is planned and requires platform agreements, SDKs, hardware, and dedicated work.
limitations: No platform implementation or certification evidence

website.title: Planned, not implemented
bullets: Requires NDA SDKs and dev kits
No public support claim is valid today

capabilities.name: C++ module runtime
capabilities.summary: C++23 and the dynamic module lifecycle are the primary engine and gameplay extension path.
limitations: Real shared-library lifecycle, ABI compatibility, packaged loading, and hot reload need stronger release gates across every module

website.title: The primary implementation path
bullets: C++ owns the full runtime surface
Dynamic modules expose a shared lifecycle
Packaged loading, ABI/versioning, and hot-reload proof remain release work

capabilities.name: NullRHI headless runtime
capabilities.summary: NullRHI is a deliberate no-render device path for headless servers, automation, and GPU-less execution.
limitations: Packaged-server soak, load, shutdown, leak, crash, and operations evidence is not yet a blocking release lane

website.title: A real no-render path
bullets: No GPU device is required
Useful for tests and dedicated servers
Package, soak, load, and recovery gates still apply

capabilities.name: Direct3D 11
capabilities.summary: D3D11 is the deepest and intended primary rendered path on Windows.
limitations: Same-commit packaged golden scenes, performance budgets, driver coverage, and release evidence remain open

website.title: The primary renderer candidate
bullets: Carries the broadest renderer integration
Windows is the intended host
Golden-scene, performance, driver, and packaging evidence still gate release

capabilities.name: Direct3D 12
capabilities.summary: D3D12 contains substantial modern-feature work but is not certified feature-for-feature against the primary renderer.
limitations: Pass parity, synchronization, shader tooling, golden scenes, performance, and driver coverage remain incomplete

website.title: Modern features, parity unproven
bullets: Mesh shader, ray tracing, and VRS surfaces exist
Pass parity, synchronization, shader tooling, drivers, and performance need certification

capabilities.name: Vulkan
capabilities.summary: Vulkan has a substantive backend and deterministic parity hooks, while full production pass execution and GPU readback parity remain incomplete.
limitations: Full GPU golden-scene readback, every production pass variant, and hard shader-toolchain dependencies are not closed

website.title: A substantial experimental backend
bullets: Dynamic rendering and parity milestones exist
Full pass execution, GPU readback, shader tools, drivers, and performance remain open

capabilities.name: OpenGL
capabilities.summary: OpenGL provides a portable and software-renderable backend, but production visual parity and supported driver coverage are not certified.
limitations: HLSL translation limitations, driver matrix, golden scenes, performance, and packaged runtime proof remain open

website.title: Portable and experimental
bullets: Hardware and llvmpipe paths are useful for portability
Translation, driver, visual parity, performance, and package gates remain open

capabilities.name: Metal
capabilities.summary: Metal is an incomplete backend surface and must not be presented as feature-complete or supported.
limitations: Backend implementation, shader path, pass parity, resource lifetime, golden scenes, performance, and packaged macOS proof remain open

website.title: Parity work, not a release backend
bullets: An API surface exists
Complete command, resource, shader, pass, test, performance, and packaging work remains

capabilities.name: Authoritative multiplayer toolkit
capabilities.summary: Transport, replication, prediction, reconciliation, lag rewind, and dedicated-server systems form a serious toolkit, but real hostile multi-client and compatibility gates are missing.
limitations: Credentials can cross the protocol in plaintext
Transport security is placeholder-grade
Existing tests often mirror logic instead of running independent production clients

website.title: A real toolkit with production boundaries
bullets: Authority, replication, prediction, reconciliation, and lag rewind exist
Secure transport, independent clients, compatibility, load, persistence, and operations remain blocking

capabilities.name: Production online services
capabilities.summary: SparkEngine does not provide a turnkey production identity, matchmaking, fleet, transactional persistence, abuse, billing, or incident-operations service layer.
limitations: Local and reference implementations are not a production control plane

website.title: Product infrastructure remains product work
bullets: Identity, matchmaking, fleet, persistence, abuse, telemetry, backups, and incident response need an explicit service program

capabilities.name: Packaged single-player runtime
capabilities.summary: The core runtime can support bounded local games, while packaged content, save compatibility, crash, performance, and installer gates still determine release readiness.
limitations: No complete end-to-end editor-to-cooked-package release certification

website.title: The narrowest release path
bullets: Avoids external service requirements
Still requires a complete author-cook-package-install-run-save-upgrade loop

capabilities.name: AngelScript gameplay runtime
capabilities.summary: The VM, bindings, modules, and entity APIs exist, but a complete entity lifecycle and integrated physics/audio/animation/event path is not wired into the runtime.
limitations: No production caller for the full start/update/collision lifecycle
Entity injection and several gameplay bindings are incomplete or log-only

website.title: Functional integration with lifecycle debt
bullets: VM, bindings, isolation, and compile paths exist
Entity identity, dispatch, subsystem APIs, hot reload, diagnostics, and packaging need end-to-end proof

capabilities.name: Visual scripting
capabilities.summary: The graph and AngelScript generation surfaces exist, while runtime execution, diagnostics, migration, source mapping, and packaged authoring are incomplete.
limitations: Depends on the unfinished AngelScript runtime lifecycle
The VisualScript module can appear loaded without a compiled gameplay loop

website.title: An authoring surface awaiting runtime closure
bullets: Graph and code-generation work exist
Execution, diagnostics, migration, hot reload, packaging, and gameplay acceptance remain open

capabilities.name: SparkEditor authoring workflow
capabilities.summary: SparkEditor contains a broad real tool surface, while command-backed editing, full gizmos, typed asset workflows, cooking, and packaged round trips need closure.
limitations: Some hierarchy/inspector changes bypass undo
Rotate/scale gizmo and real asset-thumbnail/drag paths are incomplete

website.title: A substantial workbench with workflow gaps
bullets: Scene, content, graph, profiler, and specialized panels exist
Undo discipline, gizmos, asset UX, cook/package, migration, and integration tests need closure

capabilities.name: MMOFPS / TERRAFRONT
capabilities.summary: The deepest reference module is an advanced pre-release vertical slice, not a production MMO service or release-certified game.
limitations: No encrypted production transport
No true two-independent-client acceptance gate
Restart, migration, transactional persistence, scale, and operations proof remain incomplete

website.title: Advanced vertical integration before production closure
bullets: Gameplay, vehicles, territory, bots, UI, persistence, and authority meet in one module
Transport, independent clients, restart, migration, scale, service operations, and release evidence remain blocking

capabilities.name: FPS reference module
capabilities.summary: FPS is a playable single-player reference slice; its multiplayer path is disconnected or fake and is not release evidence.
limitations: Fake/in-memory multiplayer state
No production two-client authoritative loop
Content and persistence gaps remain

website.title: Playable locally; multiplayer under integration
bullets: Arena, input, combat, rendering, and AI form a local slice
Authoritative remote players, real-source tests, assets, and persistence need closure

capabilities.name: Genre prototype modules
capabilities.summary: MMO, ARPG, RPG, RTS, Racing, Platformer, OpenWorld, VisualScript, and the base SparkGame are currently templates, showcases, or prototypes rather than MMOFPS-equivalent finished modules.
limitations: Most depend on in-memory/debug models
Several lack real assets, input, ECS/physics/render integration, persistence, or production-source tests

website.title: A template and prototype portfolio to finish
bullets: Each genre has a concrete source foothold
Lifecycle, gameplay, assets, persistence, tests, and declared N/A dimensions must reach its release profile

gates.name: Source-of-truth integrity
gates.summary: The validated readiness contract now owns public status and metrics, while stale repository documentation generators still prevent this gate from passing.
acceptanceCriteria: One validated readiness contract owns public status
All numeric claims are generated
Documentation health is current
Regeneration is deterministic and clean

gates.name: Fail-closed CI evidence
gates.summary: Required jobs can mask failures or remain advisory; docs-only changes can bypass the engine evidence path.
acceptanceCriteria: Required commands propagate failure
Every Working commit receives normalized evidence
Advisory lanes are not represented as support gates
JUnit and gate summaries attach to the exact SHA

gates.name: Supported build matrix
gates.summary: The intended configurations and module/tool targets are not all built as required, reproducible gates.
acceptanceCriteria: Declared host/compiler configurations configure and build from clean checkout
Every shipped target and real module library is built
Shipping configuration exists and is distinct from Debug/Release
Submodule/toolchain inputs are pinned

gates.name: Production-source test coverage
gates.summary: Many module tests compile subsets or mirrored logic rather than packaged production implementations; coverage thresholds are nonblocking.
acceptanceCriteria: Every real module library loads and executes in tests
No mirror-only or tautological test satisfies release
Coverage thresholds are explicit and enforced
Sanitizer and concurrency lanes fail closed

gates.name: Asset, cook, and package integrity
gates.summary: Missing and case-mismatched assets, repository-relative paths, and unvalidated package content prevent release confidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Every module has a validated content manifest
Zero missing or case-mismatched references
Cooked packages launch without repository-relative dependencies
Package smoke tests cover clean machines

gates.name: Versioned Shipping artifacts
gates.summary: No tag or release is published; the workflow emits Debug/Release rather than a version-injected hardened Shipping configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: Version is derived from the tag and embedded everywhere
Shipping artifacts are deterministic
Installer/uninstaller/upgrade/rollback smoke tests pass
Release notes and compatibility policy are published

gates.name: Supply-chain integrity
gates.summary: Release artifacts lack signing, checksums, SBOM, provenance, and enforced dependency/license policy.
acceptanceCriteria: Every artifact is signed and checksummed
SBOM and provenance are attached
Third-party license/manifest validation is blocking
Dependency and CodeQL findings follow an owned severity policy

gates.name: Security and hostile-input safety
gates.summary: Network authentication can traverse plaintext fields, placeholder crypto remains, and parser/protocol fuzz gates are incomplete.
acceptanceCriteria: Threat model and security ownership are current
Authenticated encryption, replay protection, rotation, bounds, and version negotiation pass
Credentials never appear in captures/logs/dumps
Network, asset, save, and script fuzzers meet budgets

gates.name: Platform support certification
gates.summary: Support labels are not backed by installable packages, system tests, and owned matrices at the same commit.
acceptanceCriteria: Every supported platform has a declared compiler/OS/device matrix
Build, install, launch, content, input, audio, crash, save, upgrade, and uninstall pass
Experimental and unsupported targets remain labeled

gates.name: Renderer parity and visual correctness
gates.summary: The primary renderer and experimental backends lack a shared packaged golden-scene, pass, shader, synchronization, driver, and performance certification matrix.
acceptanceCriteria: D3D11 primary scene suite passes
Each supported backend meets its declared pass subset and visual thresholds
Skinned glTF import works
GPU captures and budgets attach to the tested SHA

gates.name: Runtime and editor workflow closure
gates.summary: Core pieces exist, but full lifecycle, undo-safe authoring, cook/package, hot reload, crash, and clean shutdown are not one enforced workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: Create-edit-save-reload-cook-package-install-run round trip passes
All editor world changes are command-backed
Module and resource lifetimes shut down cleanly
Packaged runtime emits actionable crash evidence

gates.name: Gameplay scripting closure
gates.summary: AngelScript and visual scripting do not yet provide a complete, safe, debuggable, migratable packaged gameplay lifecycle.
acceptanceCriteria: Start/update/fixed/destroy/collision/trigger/event dispatch is real
Physics/audio/animation/input/EventBus bindings work
Hot reload follows documented state rules
Graph diagnostics and source mapping reach packaged runtime

gates.name: Production multiplayer and services
gates.summary: True independent-client, secure transport, compatibility, persistence, scale, recovery, and operations gates are missing.
acceptanceCriteria: Dedicated server plus two independent clients pass authoritative gameplay
Protocol compatibility and hostile-client suites pass
Transactional persistence and restart/migration recovery pass
Load, telemetry, alerts, backups, and incident drills meet budgets

gates.name: Game-module release profiles
gates.summary: Only MMOFPS approaches a deep vertical slice; FPS is local-playable and the remaining modules are prototypes/templates with uneven real-source tests and assets.
acceptanceCriteria: Every discovered module has a validated manifest and declared N/A dimensions
Applicable lifecycle/gameplay/assets/persistence/AI/editor/tests reach score 3
Modules are packaged and smoke-tested
Prototype/template labels are generated from the contract

gates.name: Performance, reliability, and operations
gates.summary: Profilers exist, while representative budgets, long soaks, leak limits, crash symbolization, service telemetry, alerting, backups, and recovery drills are not release gates.
acceptanceCriteria: Representative CPU/GPU/memory/load budgets are versioned
Long soaks show bounded memory and tick/frame percentiles
Crashes produce symbolized actionable reports
Backups, restore, rollback, and incident drills pass

gates.name: Documentation, legal, and support truth
gates.summary: Website wording is generated from the tested contract, while documentation generators, clean-machine quick starts, and release legal/support review remain incomplete.
acceptanceCriteria: Docs health is current and every link resolves
License, attribution, trademark, privacy, security, support, and contribution text is reviewed for the release
Quick starts run from clean machines
Website wording is generated from the tested contract

gates.name: Compatibility and migration
gates.summary: SDK ABI, module, save, asset, protocol, and editor-data compatibility policies and migration tests are incomplete.
acceptanceCriteria: Version contracts exist for SDK, modules, assets, saves, scenes, protocols, and scripts
N-1 upgrade and rollback fixtures pass
Breaking changes fail with actionable diagnostics
Release notes enumerate migrations

gates.name: Release rehearsal and sign-off
gates.summary: No tagged release has rehearsed every blocking gate, artifact, install, migration, rollback, documentation, and support step at one commit.
acceptanceCriteria: A release candidate tag passes all blocking gates
Artifacts are installed and upgraded on clean supported hosts
Rollback and recovery drills pass
Owners sign the evidence ledger before the final tag

rules: Start only work items whose dependencies are done; parallelize every independent item in the same wave.
Keep implementation, production-source tests, documentation, readiness status, generated handoff, and website impact in one change.
Do not close an item from comments or screenshots alone; execute its commands and attach exact-SHA CI evidence.
If acceptance reveals a new blocker, add a stable work-item ID and dependency before expanding scope.
Never weaken a gate to make it pass. Fix the implementation, evidence path, or public claim.
At the end of each session, regenerate the handoff and leave the first unblocked item explicit.
